newsitem.title: FINLAND: HELSINKI BOURSE SEES REMOTE ACCESS BOOSTING TRADE.
newsitem.headline: HELSINKI BOURSE SEES REMOTE ACCESS BOOSTING TRADE.

text.p: The Helsinki Stock Exchange said on Monday it expects remote access to boost trade in Finnish shares on the bourse and to reduce companies' need to list their shares on overseas exchanges.
"Through remote membership (in the bourse), trading in shares will more and more concentrate on the home bourse," the stock exchange said in a statement.

"Already with the existing technology, Helsinki Stock Exchange is able to provide services to international investors that will make it unnecessary for Finnish companies to seek listing on other European stock exchanges," it said.
Last June, Danish banking group Den Danske Bank was accepted as the first foreign remote broker on the Helsinki bourse.
The bourse repeated that it planned to introduce a new trading and information system in the first half of 1998.
The Helsinki Stock Exchange in February ordered the new trading system from Australian company Computershare .
The open interface of the new system would allow it to be linked to other systems in the future, enabling cooperation with other stock exchanges, including Nordic bourses, the stock exchange said.
